selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What scene are readers asked to imagine at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: They are asked to picture themselves in a harsh pre-Islamic setting marked by ignorance, spiritual neglect, and a world seen as dull and lifeless.

questions.question: Why does the passage use the image of stars for Qur’anic verses?
questions.answer: To show that the verses shine, guide, and drive away darkness.

questions.question: What kind of world are readers first asked to imagine?
questions.answer: A world of ignorance and roughness where people fail to see the living meaning of creation.

questions.question: How are the earth, land, sea, animals, and plants described in this renewed vision?
questions.answer: The earth is portrayed like a living whole, while land, sea, animals, and plants are seen as expressing glorification.

questions.question: What literary effect is created by describing the sky, earth, and creatures as if they speak?
questions.answer: It helps the reader sense that the universe is full of meaning, expression, and testimony to Allah.

questions.question: How is the earth reimagined in the same vision?
questions.answer: It is seen as full of forms of praise, with its regions and living things serving like expressions of remembrance.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the historical spread of the verses’ light?
questions.answer: It says their light has continued from that first time onward and has become widely recognized over time.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying this is only one type among many kinds of miraculousness?
questions.answer: It means the Qur’an has multiple forms of wonder, and this passage is explaining just one of them.

questions.question: What does the phrase “among its many varieties” indicate about miraculousness?
questions.answer: It indicates that the Qur’an’s miraculous nature has many dimensions, not just one.

questions.question: What kind of darkness does the passage focus on first: physical darkness, spiritual darkness, or political darkness?
questions.answer: It focuses first on spiritual and intellectual darkness.

questions.question: In that environment, how are things in the world initially perceived?
questions.answer: They are perceived as lifeless, covered over, and disconnected from sacred meaning.

questions.question: What picture of the world exists before the Qur’anic verses are heard?
questions.answer: The world appears covered, inert, and stripped of spiritual awareness.

questions.question: How does the image of the stars change after the second verse is heard?
questions.answer: They are no longer seen as mere burning objects but as meaningful signs that point to wisdom and truth.

questions.question: What is the significance of turning stars and earthly creatures into signs of speech and praise?
questions.answer: It shows that the universe is not mute or random but full of testimony to divine wisdom.

questions.question: What larger idea is taught by these images of sky, earth, stars, and living things?
questions.answer: The whole universe is shown as a meaningful order directed toward Allah.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage warn against when reading the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It warns against reading carelessly or routinely in a way that blocks deeper appreciation.

questions.question: What kind of reading does the passage encourage?
questions.answer: It encourages reflective reading that tries to recover the first hearers’ astonishment and insight.

questions.question: What does the passage claim about the level of miraculousness it is about to explain?
questions.answer: It says the coming comparison will address one of the highest levels of the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: From what point of view are readers asked to examine the verses in this passage?
questions.answer: They are asked to view them from the perspective of people encountering them in an age of deep ignorance and spiritual roughness.

questions.question: What darkness is being removed in this comparison?
questions.answer: It is the darkness of disbelief and spiritual unawareness.

questions.question: How are the sky and stars presented after this awakening in perception?
questions.answer: The sky is pictured like a speaker, and the stars like meaningful signs that display wisdom and truth.

questions.question: What inner change happens in the minds of listeners when they hear this message?
questions.answer: Their understanding becomes awakened, and they begin to see creation as alive with worship.

questions.question: How are the heavens and stars reimagined in the passage?
questions.answer: They are reimagined as expressive and meaningful, displaying truth and wisdom instead of mere physical existence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what part of the Qur’an’s miraculous nature may be missed through a shallow reading?
questions.answer: One may miss the sweetness and force of its recitation and how each verse drives away a specific kind of darkness.

title: Reviving Effect of Verses in the Age of Ignorance
